prompt: The query in the editor has one mistake. Fix it so that it answers this question: how many customers placed their latest order in a store, and how many on the web? order_ts holds UTC time, and channel says store or web. Orders with a missing customer_id are guest orders and do not count. Each customer counts once, under the channel of the order with the latest order_ts. When two orders of a customer tie on order_ts, the lower order_id is kept. Return two columns, in this order: channel and customers. Return one row for each channel. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, check the ranking function: each customer must count once, even when two latest orders share a moment.
A ranking that gives tied orders the same number keeps both; one that numbers every row apart needs the stated tie-break as its last sort key.
starter_sql:
WITH ranked AS (  -- one row per order of a known customer
  SELECT customer_id, channel,
         RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_ts DESC) AS rn
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT channel, COUNT(*) AS customers
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1
GROUP BY channel
why_this_works: ROW_NUMBER with order_id after order_ts keeps one order per customer even when two share a moment, so each customer counts once.
